texts.preamble: Rajkamal Agro Industries vs Directorate Of Revenue Intelligence on 27 September, 2018 Author: Anant S. Dave Bench: Anant S. Dave, Biren Vaishnav C/Sca/10723/2018 Order
texts.facts: 1. The challenge in this petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India by the petitioner is to the arbitrary, high- handed and unreasonable action of the respondent no. 3 of detaining the goods of the petitioner without authority of law for alleged breach of the Food Safety And Standards Act vide detention memos dated 06.04.2018, 11.04.2018, 12.04.2018 and 13.04.2018 and thereafter seizure memo issued by respondent no. 2 on 19.04.2018. 1.1 The prayer clause no. 38 is basically to quash and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the said detention memos at Annexure 'A' collectively and also to quash and [LEAKAGE_MASK] seizure memo dated 19.04.2018 issued by respondents no. 3 & 2 respectively. 1.2 It is not in dispute that by communication dated 20.06.2018, respondent no. 4 imposed Rajkamal Agro Industries vs Directorate Of Revenue Intelligence on 27 September, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170662704/ 1 condition of furnishing bond and undertaking upon the petitioner for provisional release of goods of petitioner weighing approximately 608 Metric Tons to which the petitioner has not responded and invoked the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 228 of the Constitution of India. 2. Following are the contentions raised : (I) That the petitioner is engaged in the business of importing sesame seeds from different countries which is kept in captive use, processed and then fully exported to customers outside India and that petitioner does not sell these goods in the domestic market. It is the case of the petitioner that as per Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSSA') read with the Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011, (for short 'Licensing Regulation, 2011') earlier a license was received by the petitioner from competent authority under the FSSA, which was valid upto 17.10.2017 only. The petitioner applied for reissue of license only on 09.01.2018 for which requisite application fees were paid by him and FSSAI ID FBO17182022305793 and Application Reference No. 10180109161540157 were generated.
texts.arguments: (II) Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has relied on provisions of Section 110 of The Customs Act, 1962 namely seizure of goods, documents and things which empowers the proper officer who has reason to believe that any goods are liable to confiscation under the Customs Act, seizure may be affected of the goods. The above section according to learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner does not empower the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence authority either to seize goods or issue any seizure memo and to take further action. Section 111(d) is in Chapter XIV of The Customs Act, 1962 which provides confiscation of any improperly imported goods and any goods which are imported and attempted to be imported or are brought within the Indian customs waters for the purpose of being imported, contrary to any prohibition imposed by or under this Act or any other law for the time being in force. (III) Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner would contend that import of goods seized by the authority is neither in breach of The Customs Act, nor in violation of the FSSA. Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has taken us to Section 31 of FSSA which provides for licensing and registration of food business and that no person shall commence or carry on any food business except under a licence and sub-section (4) of Section 31 which casts duty upon the Designated Officer on receipt of an application under sub-section (3) to either grant license or after giving the applicant an opportunity of being heard and for reasons to be recorded in writing, refuse to grant a license to any applicant provided he is satisfied that it is necessary to do so in the interest of public health and copy of which shall be made available to the applicant. Section 32 is about improvement notices. (IV) The Licensing Regulation, 2011 namely Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011 framed in exercise of powers conferred by clause (o) of sub-section (2) of Section 92 read with Section 31 of Food Rajkamal Agro Industries vs Directorate Of Revenue Intelligence on 27 September, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170662704/ 2 Safety and Standards Act, 2006 in detail provides for registration and licensing of food business. By emphasizing Regulation No. 2.1.4 pertaining to process of application for license (clause 2 therein), it is submitted that even in case of an application which is found incomplete upon scrutiny, or if licensing authority requires any additional information with respect to the application, the licensing authority shall inform the applicant in writing to furnish such additional information or complete the application as the case may be, within 30 days from such notice and in case applicant fails to furnish the required information within the stipulated time of 30 days, the application for licensing shall stand rejected. (V) It is averred and submitted that upon expiry of the earlier license on 17.10.2017, the petitioner filed an application before the licensing authority on 09.01.2018 and thus the petitioner received advance authorization to import goods into India on 16.01.2018. Opposing the prayers, learned Standing Counsel Mr. Parth Bhatt would contend that unless valid license for the business of food is granted to the importer or any person, no goods can be imported. 3.1 Learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent authority invite various pleadings filed in this petition to which learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner reiterated that receipt produced was neither fake nor tampered with and affidavit filed by the Consultant of the applicant dated 08.09.2018 along with statement of account of State Bank of India reveal that application fees of Rs.37,970.45 was shown in the debit column.
